My experience with Motherhood Sarjapur management was very disappointing. The doctors are good, but the management is stressful, unprofessional, and not transparent, especially when it comes to insurance claims. Staff behavior was rude at times, particularly if you opted for insurance, and it felt like extra charges were added without proper clarification. They charged around ₹1.7 lakh even for a normal delivery.

Their ambulance service was also pathetic. We waited for more than 3 hours, and in the end, we had to arrange our own transport. Overall, the management is not reliable or trustworthy. Please verify all billing and insurance details carefully before proceeding.

Disclaimer: This 1-star rating is specifically for the counselling and billing experience, and NOT for the doctors or nursing staff.

We recently had our delivery at Motherhood Hospital, Sarjapur. While the medical care itself was excellent, I am giving a 1-star rating specifically due to my experience with the counselling and billing process.

Dr. Deepmala and the entire medical team were excellent, supportive, and highly professional. The nursing staff and support teams were also extremely caring and attentive, which made a big difference during such an important time.

However, our experience with the counselling team was quite disappointing, especially with Puja Das and Gargi. The package details were not explained clearly, and there was a significant lack of transparency in the billing structure. It felt like the focus was more on selling packages and pre-booking beds rather than providing clear and accurate information to patients.

Despite repeated follow-ups, we did not receive a proper breakup of non-medical expenses, which caused unnecessary confusion and frustration.

I strongly recommend the hospital for its doctors and medical care, but there is a serious need for improvement in the counselling and billing transparency process.

reviews.snippet:
Disclaimer: This 1-star rating is specifically for the package counselling, room infrastructure and billing experience, and NOT for the doctors or nursing staff.

We recently had our delivery at Motherhood Hospital, Sarjapur. While the medical care itself was excellent, I am giving a 1-star rating specifically due to my experience with the counselling and billing process.

Dr. Deepmala and the entire medical team were excellent, supportive, and highly professional. The nursing staff and support teams were also extremely caring and attentive, which made a big difference during such an important time.

However, our experience with the counselling team was quite disappointing. The package details were changed what I have signed up for an booked the bed. There was a significant lack of transparency in the billing structure. The change in GIPSA package in the mid of year has caused an unnecessary headache at a critical time. The insurance TPA mediassist is informing that the package is still the same which has caused me loosing money even after paying significant amount to the insurance company as premium. The package team didn't tell clearly to the billing team what all things are provided as complementary when we signed up for the package. I felt like the focus was more on selling packages and pre-booking beds rather than providing clear and accurate information to patients.

The MoU between insurance company and hospital can change any time to increase your medical bills. Please read all the consumables and counselling such as lactation, physio etc as billing team will be charging them even they are included in the package.

Please take all your consulting paper printout from them as they will be helpful while claiming pre and post medical expenses. Motherhood doesn't upload prescription on App as it is not necessary from their perspective.

The billing team at ground floor can also try getting charges for emergency though that was not even the case. Please be mindful of that.

We did receive a proper breakup of non-medical expenses and the returned one were not even deducted from the billing. Please take a proper note of that.

I have been allocated room number 202. The room needs a lot of improvement. I believe the renovation is going on, but they need to provide rooms which has hot water facilities. The shelf are broken in few rooms. The room can be changed as per the availability and customer experience team is supporting in that.

Food seems to be fine, but it doesn't look like nutritionaist approved.

I strongly recommend the hospital for its doctors and medical care, but the billing and management needs to work on transparency and clear communication with the attenders. They need to understand the family is going through a very critical time. There is a serious need for improvement in the counselling and billing transparency process.

I want to tell the management, the experience is not just doctor and nursing staff's responsibility. How do you support the family at that time, will be remembered.

reviews.snippet:
My experience with Dr. Divya Chandrasekar at Motherhood Hospital was extremely disheartening, especially during such a sensitive and emotional phase of life—pregnancy. I had been consulting her throughout my pregnancy, but the way she treated me and my family during the later stages left a lasting negative impact.

When I informed her during my 7th month check-up that I would be travelling to my hometown for delivery, her reaction was unexpectedly harsh. Instead of offering support or guidance, she began scolding my elderly parents in front of me, warning us of possible complications in a manner that felt more like a curse than medical advice. She started telling if we travel at this month we'll end up with preterm delivery.This deeply upset my family, especially my parents, who were simply looking out for me.

We had consulted a senior and experienced doctor in our hometown (a 70-year-old with decades of experience) who assured us that travel was safe at that stage. When we mentioned this, Dr. Divya seemed visibly offended and her attitude toward us changed drastically. It felt like she was more concerned about the fact that we were not delivering at Motherhood than about my wellbeing as a patient.

This experience made the final stretch of my pregnancy extremely stressful. What should have been a time of support and encouragement turned into emotional distress. I felt judged, unsupported, and cornered—all during a time when mental peace and emotional stability are crucial.

Thankfully, I reached my hometown safely and delivered a healthy, beautiful baby boy on my expected due date, under the care of the very doctor she had dismissed.

My sincere advice to expecting mothers: if you are not planning to deliver at Motherhood Hospital, or if you value emotional support along with medical care, I would not recommend consulting with Dr. Divya Chandrasekar. Every pregnant woman deserves compassion, respect, and unbiased care—especially during such a precious journey.

If you care for your family avoid motherhood at all cost.
My experience at motherhood wasn’t great at all. Reasons for this was below:
1: Multiple scans suggested by doctor, when the pregnancy was going normal compared to their competitors like cloudnine.
2: The doctors at night duty and the main doctor wasn’t responsible at all, my baby’s heart rate dropped and she wasn’t coming to check even after nurse calling her repeatedly. The baby was in distress for very long time all i had was a nurse who had no clue what to do.
3: They inflate the bill for consumables so much that it becomes much more than the estimation they give initially.
4: Some tests weren’t done but still added to the bill, on calling out they called it as a “mistake”

One thing that I appreciate will be team of nurses who are ready to help you out after delivery 24*7 and always on their toes. But overall not considering motherhood again or won’t recommend to anyone else.

Visited this hospital just for Dr. Teena Thomas who is just amazing ! She is the best doctor I hv seen ever.

But coming to my delivery, this hospitals has the worst and careless nurses.

Next is about billing folks who behave as if we are taking treatment for free. Such arrogance and attitude when we ask some query. I am not sure why these kind of frustrated people are made to sit in counter.

I could write a book of issues with this hospital staying just for 2 days !!!!

Pathetic Hospital but again to repeat

DR. TEENA THOMAS IS THE BEST !! Its because of her we wer blessed with a healthy baby. She has guided me from day 1 and ensure that my preganancy journey to be smooth.

reviews.snippet:
I'd gladly give these incompetents a negative star on Google if I could. It's been an agonizing 19 months, and the trauma from this disastrous experience still haunts us. These people are nothing short of formula milk fanatics, practically shoving it down your throat like it's the elixir of life.

On my floor, it's like a twisted formula assembly line, with every newborn force-fed 30 ml of that formula every two hours. Breastfeeding? Forget about it. They won't lift a finger to help you initiate it, but they're quick to terrorize you with horror stories about your baby's glucose levels tanking if you don't succumb to their formula-pushing tactics.

And let's not overlook their magnificent ability to screw up the basics. In some absurd newborn screening test (that, mind you, we had to pay for), they managed to misidentify the gender. Bravo, genius! It's like amateur hour in a supposed medical facility.

Oh, and everyone there thinks they're a doctor. Even the janitor fancies himself a formula expert, eagerly dishing out unsolicited advice like it's going out of style. The lactation therapist, bless her heart, decides to grace you with her presence a whopping two days after delivery – conveniently when the formula stock needs replenishing. Coincidence? I think not.

And if you dare to stick to your guns and insist on exclusive breastfeeding, prepare to be treated like a pariah. No proper discharge from the observation room, no help initiating feeding, and heaven forbid you ask a nurse for assistance – you'll be met with disdainful looks and eye rolls.

I'll begrudgingly admit that the delivery and c-section procedures were handled competently, and I won't nitpick on that front. However, the post-delivery pediatric care, especially when it comes to breastfeeding, is nothing short of pathetic.

In a nutshell, this place is a breeding ground for formula-mongering quacks who care more about their profit margins than the well-being of newborns and their mothers. Avoid like the plague.

And let's not overlook their magnificent ability to screw up the basics. In some absurd newborn screening test (that, mind you, we had to pay for), they managed to misidentify the gender. Bravo, genius! It's like amateur hour in a supposed medical facility.

Oh, and everyone there thinks they're a doctor. Even the janitor fancies himself a formula expert, eagerly dishing out unsolicited advice like it's going out of style. The lactation therapist, bless her heart, decides to grace you with her presence a whopping two days after delivery – conveniently when the formula stock needs replenishing. Coincidence? I think not.

And if you dare to stick to your guns and insist on exclusive breastfeeding, prepare to be treated like a pariah. No proper discharge from the observation room, no help initiating feeding, and heaven forbid you ask a nurse for assistance – you'll be met with disdainful looks and eye rolls.

I'll begrudgingly admit that the delivery and c-section procedures were handled competently, and I won't nitpick on that front. However, the post-delivery pediatric care, especially when it comes to breastfeeding, is nothing short of pathetic.

In a nutshell, this place is a breeding ground for formula-mongering quacks who care more about their profit margins than the well-being of newborns and their mothers. Avoid like the plague.

Highly disappointed with Dr. Sangeetha Gomes and Motherhood hospital. I was consulting Dr. Shefali until now who has been wonderful throughout my journey. She moved to a different hospital and Motherhood assigned Dr. Sangeetha to me for a consultation. Throughout my conversation with her, I felt she was trying to ensure that I get a preterm birth so she can make money. She said things like if baby's weight is between 2.5 to 2.8 kg only then she would go for normal delivery, otherwise c-sec. She recommended a few things which were highly controversial. I did check with a few other folks as well and everyone was shocked (to say the least) at her recommendations. I'll only request you to please do your due diligence before approaching this doctor.
Also, for the Motherhood hospital, the staff who had my file, removed all my previous doctor's prescriptions, my weight and BP chart, and all the bills that I was maintaining without asking me. I can understand that this must be a human mistake, I just hope for a better way to manage this.

I really had a bad experience with motherhood. Had been there for pregnancy consultation and delivery.

The medicals doesn't have the prescribed medecine most of the time.

I delivered a baby at 12pm and was shifted to ward by around 6pm ,when we escalated this to the management they said they have no rooms and working on it. They didn't allow my family members to see me or my baby until i was shifted to the ward.
I was not provided with proper food or water for almost more than 12hrs after delivery. The staff management is so poor and the nursing staff won't be available when needed and few nursing staffs are so arrogant and they won't take care of us.

They'll prescribe you for unnecessary tests and consultation and everything gets added to the total bill. Even though they do certain tests they won't show the report to you saying that doctors will take care you don't need to worry , don't you think we have the rights to view the test reports and decide accordingly??? They do all test on the day of discharge and they said your baby has jaundice u need to stay for couple of more days and they started the treatment without showing us the reports and we had to pay additional charges for all of these.
The billing management and the reception staffs and lab staff are all so irresponsible they don't value their patients time and they'll stretch the discharge process as much as they can to charge you more post discharge hours.

Pathetic experience and I highly don't recommend this hospital for any kind of treatment. Other small Private hospitals and govt hospital are far better than your services

I had my previous experience and Manipal and it was way way better . If one is looking for post delivery service - would not recommend this place at all.
